channels.commands.usage:
`/the-loop help` — this text
`/the-loop <keyword> <work-item> [@login] [instance:<name>]` — a control keyword on a work item (`start`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `execute`, `contribute`, `do`, `review`, `cleanup`, `add-collaborator @login`, `remove-collaborator @login`); the work item is `github:owner/repo#N`, `owner/repo#N`, `#N` (against kickoff.repo) or its GitHub URL
`/the-loop new [<repo>:] <title>` — open a work item (the kickoff's grammar: a first-line `<repo>:` prefix against the declared `repositories`, else `kickoff.repo`; more lines are the body); its thread opens here
`/the-loop status` · `/the-loop restart` · `/the-loop upgrade` — this instance
`/the-loop standing list` · `/the-loop standing start|stop|restart <name>` — standing sessions

channels.verbs.help:
*Addressing the-loop* — mention it, then one of:
• `record-context` (in a thread) — snapshot this thread onto the work item as context
• `record-decision [product|design|tech:] <text> [— why: <rationale>]` — record a decision (authorized users only)
• `add-collaborator @login` or `slack:U…` — let that person feed this work item (authorized users only)
• `start`, `execute`, … — any control keyword's last word (authorized users only)
• `execute without 1, 3` or `skip <phase>` — execute with those phases of the checklist unticked (authorized users only)
• `help` — this text, shown only to you; `help public` — the same as a reply everyone here can see
• anything else — a reply, delivered to the session as input

eventlog.event-type.aggregate.partial: A list read on a manager answered without every member (operation, left_out). Debug level: the response header `The-Loop-Instances-Unreachable` and `GET /api/v1/instances` carry the same fact for clients.
eventlog.event-type.api.request: One control-plane API operation completed (method, path, status). Every mutating and reading route lands here; /health is exempt. Debug level (issue-283): a polling dashboard's own reads must not drown the events an operator reads the log for.
eventlog.event-type.arm.refused: A work item was not armed (work_item, reason). reason=mirror: a Jira copy labelled the-loop-mirror — the GitHub issue it mirrors runs the loop (issue-517). Settled, never retried.
eventlog.event-type.bus.published: An event went through the bus (event_type, work_item, source, recorded: whether the ledger wrote it — null when the catalog says it is not recorded, posted: how many channels took it, channels). Debug level: one line per event, ids only.
eventlog.event-type.bus.record_failed: The ledger could not write an event (ledger, work_item, event_type, source, error). Best-effort by contract: the publisher decides what it means — the ask still reports its exit code, a reply still delivers.
eventlog.event-type.bus.recorded: The ledger wrote an event that originated elsewhere (ledger, work_item, event_type, source, url) — a comment with an envelope, or the issue a `work-item.create` opened. Always before any other channel sees it.
eventlog.event-type.channel.attachments: A forwarded Slack message carried files (issue-416): how many the message attached and how many were fetched into the work item's attachment directory for the session to read (channel, work_item, actor, count, fetched). A file that was not fetched is named on the record and in the pane with its reason; this line carries no file name and no path.
eventlog.event-type.channel.caught_up: The Socket Mode listener ran one read cycle over the bound threads and the kickoff cursor right after connecting (replies, processed, delivered, created, dropped) — issue-334. What accumulated while no listener was connected is processed once, from the shared cursors; a Slack retry of a message the catch-up already handled is dropped as `duplicate`.
eventlog.event-type.channel.command_answ: The ephemeral answer to a slash command could not be posted through its response_url (channel, actor, error) — issue-334. The outcome stands; only the member's receipt was lost.
eventlog.event-type.channel.command_comp: A slash command was acted on (channel, actor, family, verb, work_item or standing, outcome: recorded | record-failed | ok | failed) — issue-334. `recorded` means the ledger holds the control keyword and its ingress executes it next; `ok` means the core facade returned.
eventlog.event-type.channel.command_rece: An authorized member's `/the-loop` slash command passed the grant check (channel, actor: the member id, family: work-item | instance | standing, verb, target: the resolved work-item ref or the standing name) — issue-334. Ids only, never the command text.
eventlog.event-type.channel.context_reco: A `record-context` act landed: the thread's snapshot was written to the ticket as a marked context record (channel, work_item, actor, thread, count: messages in the snapshot) — issue-389 R3.
eventlog.event-type.channel.created: A top-level channel message became a work item (channel, work_item: the new ref, actor, thread) — the `work-item.create` grant (issue-309). The issue is the ledger's record; the thread is bound to it.
eventlog.event-type.channel.decision_rec: A `record-decision` act landed: the decision text was written to the ticket as a marked decision record (channel, work_item, actor, thread, kind: the keyword when one closed the act) — issue-389 R4.
eventlog.event-type.channel.delivered_la: A queued event was accepted by a channel on a later attempt and left the outbox (event_type, work_item, attempts, waited_seconds) — issue-409.
eventlog.event-type.channel.dropped: An inbound channel message was not processed (reason: unmapped | self-authored | unauthorized-actor | undeliverable | unpublishable-event | kickoff-unknown-repo | kickoff-ambiguous-repo | kickoff-no-target | kickoff-empty-message | create-failed | unknown-command | unknown-target | duplicate | channel-disabled | unknown-phase | unskippable-phase | empty-clause | checklist-unreadable; channel, work_item, actor, kind: the classified event type — or, for a refused kickoff, the repository prefix that was read, error; read: for a refused `execute without` reply, the items the clause was read as, a word that is not a name as its length only, issue-405). The four selection reasons are a typed phase-selection reply refused (issue-393 R9.3): a name, number or word the checklist does not offer, a protected phase, a clause naming nothing, and a checklist that could not be read just then (transient, retriable). undeliverable means the mirror stood but no session could take the reply; unpublishable-event means the message classified as a type the channel's `publish` list does not grant (issue-309) — dropped, never downgraded. The four `kickoff-` reasons are a top-level message whose target could not be settled (issue-341): a prefix naming nothing declared, one naming several, no prefix and no `kickoff.repo` fallback, and a prefix with no message after it — each answered in the member's own thread, never guessed. The last three are the slash command's (issue-334): text outside its vocabulary, a work item this instance is not configured for, a trigger already handled.
eventlog.event-type.channel.heartbeat: The Socket Mode listener received one of `the-loop doctor slack`'s own heartbeat messages (channel_id, ts, nonce) — issue-393 F2. The doctor posts a fixed-format nonce into the configured channel and counts how many reach this listener within its window; a shortfall is EVIDENCE (Slack lists no connections, so never proof) that a second Socket Mode consumer shares the app token and Slack is splitting events between them. A heartbeat never enters the inbound pipeline.
eventlog.event-type.channels.short_form_: A session-authored event reached Slack without a short form (work_item, event_type, event_id), so the channel built one from the first question or sentence — issue-549 R3.4. Carries no message text.
eventlog.event-type.channel.kickoff_aske: A top-level channel message could not be resolved to a repository, so the-loop ASKED which one (channel, actor, thread, kind: the unresolved outcome, count: how many repositories were offered) — issue-349. Nothing was created, recorded or bound: the message is held until the member picks, or until the question expires. Ids and counts only, never the message text and never a repository name.
eventlog.event-type.channel.mirror_faile: The work-item mirror of a channel reply could not be posted (channel, work_item, error); the delivery attempt still proceeds.
eventlog.event-type.channel.mirror_skipp: A channel reply had no work item to mirror onto and was delivered anyway (channel, work_item, reason: standing-session) — a standing session owns no ticket, so this event IS its paper trail (issue-277).
eventlog.event-type.channel.mirrored: A channel reply was posted onto its work item as the-loop's own marker-stamped comment — the single-source-of-truth rule (channel, work_item, actor).
eventlog.event-type.channel.open_failed: A work item started but a channel could not open its conversation (channel, work_item, error) — issue-317. Best-effort by contract: the session was spawned regardless, nothing was bound, and the next event for the work item opens the thread lazily as before issue-317.
eventlog.event-type.channel.post_failed: A channel post failed (channel, work_item, event_type, error) — best-effort by contract: the ask's outcome is unaffected and the work item remains the record.
eventlog.event-type.channel.posted: An outbound event was posted to a communication channel (channel, work_item, event_type, thread: the provider's conversation handle) — issue-245. The work item already carries the text; this is the fan-out.
eventlog.event-type.channel.posting_unav: `the-loop start` found Slack enabled and no way to post to it (reason: the unset bot-token variable and, with a gateway block, what the gateway said about `slack.post.enabled` or that it could not be asked) — issue-519. Warning level, once per start; the start itself succeeds and a failed post waits in the outbox.
eventlog.event-type.channel.press_report: The Slack channel could not edit the pressed message to show the press's outcome (channel, work_item, thread, action, error) — issue-337. Best-effort by contract: the record and the reactions are unaffected. A message the bot did not post (`cant_update_message`) is the usual cause.

The Slack channel wrote a button press's outcome onto the pressed message (channel, work_item, thread, action: the action_id the-loop rendered, outcome: landed | failed) — issue-337. `landed` means the pressed buttons were removed and the line links the record; `failed` means the buttons stayed beside the error. Ids only, never the value.
eventlog.event-type.channel.gate_closed: The Slack channel edited a gate's message after the gate was answered (channel, work_item, node, outcome: the gate's outcome, edited: true | false, error) — issue-549 R11.6. The edit shows the outcome and who answered and removes the buttons; `edited: false` means Slack refused the edit, and the gate itself is unaffected.
eventlog.event-type.channel.reaction_add: The Slack channel acknowledged an accepted inbound message with a reaction on that message (channel, work_item, state: received | completed | error, content: the emoji name, thread) — issue-325, channels.slack.reactions. Debug level: the decoration mirrors reaction.added on GitHub. Ids and names only, never text.
eventlog.event-type.channel.reaction_fai: The Slack channel could not add an acknowledgment reaction (channel, work_item, state, content, thread, error) — issue-325. Best-effort by contract: the record and the delivery are unaffected. A missing reactions:write scope on the bot token is the usual cause.
eventlog.event-type.channel.reply_receiv: An authorized reply arrived through a channel and entered the pipeline (channel, work_item, actor: the channel-native member id, kind: the event type it became, gate: open | none | unknown — what the graph read returned, issue-321). Payloads carry ids, never message text.
eventlog.event-type.channel.shortcut_fai: The Slack channel could not open the decision modal or answer the shortcut's member (channel, error) — issue-389 R6. Best-effort by contract: the member sees nothing and can type the mention instead.
eventlog.event-type.channel.shortcut_rec: A message shortcut arrived over Socket Mode (channel, work_item, actor: Slack member id, shortcut: the callback id) — issue-389 R6. It is handled exactly as the typed mention would be.
eventlog.event-type.channel.snapshot_emp: A `record-context` act found nothing new since the thread's last snapshot, so no record was written (channel, work_item, thread) — issue-389 R3. The member is told in the thread.
eventlog.event-type.channel.split_cleare: A split check came back clean after one or more short ones (channel, channel_id, beats, echoed, after: how many consecutive short checks it ends) — issue-413. Closes the warning ladder that channel.split_suspected opened. It does not mean the split is gone: at two beats a real split answers clean a quarter of the time, which is why `status` reads the rolling window rather than this one verdict.
eventlog.event-type.channel.split_suspec: The Socket Mode listener's own split check heard back fewer heartbeats than it posted (channel, channel_id, beats, echoed, window_seconds, consecutive: how many checks in a row have now been short, remedy) — issue-413. Warning level: roughly half of everything inbound — mentions, presses, slash commands — is landing on another Socket Mode consumer holding the same app-level token, and the loss is otherwise visible only as an ABSENCE (no channel.dropped, no record at all). EVIDENCE, never proof: Slack exposes no API that lists an app's connections. Emitted on the first short check and then once every SPLIT_ESCALATE_EVERY, so a persistent split is a periodic warning and not a storm.
eventlog.event-type.channel.thread_opene: A conversation was bound to a work item (channel, work_item, thread: the root's ts, channel_id, origin: event | kickoff | start) — issue-312. `event` means the-loop opened a root for the first event it delivered; `kickoff` means a member's top-level message became the work item and that thread is its conversation; `start` means the-loop opened the root when the work item started, before any event (issue-317); `declared` means it was re-opened in a room the work item declared (issue-375). With `mode: channel` (issue-378) the conversation is the room itself, `thread` is empty and every update is a top-level message there. Otherwise every later message is a reply into it. Ids only, never text.
eventlog.event-type.channel.undelivered: The bus asked at least one channel to take an event and NONE accepted it, so the event was queued for redelivery (event_type, work_item, channels: the ones asked, error: the first refusal, pending: how many entries the outbox now holds) — issue-409. Warning level: before this the fact lived only in a debug `bus.published` line with `posted: 0`, which is how three days of agent questions went missing. Ids and counts only; the message text is in the outbox, never in the log.
eventlog.event-type.channel.undelivered_: The outbox was full and its OLDEST entry was dropped to make room (work_item, event_type, queued_at, cap) — issue-409. The event is gone from the queue; the work item still carries whatever the ledger recorded.
eventlog.event-type.channel.view_submitt: The decision modal was submitted (channel, work_item, actor: Slack member id, kind: the keyword chosen, if any) — issue-389 R6. The text then goes through the same `record-decision` path.
eventlog.event-type.ci.autofix_exhausted: A CI check failed on more distinct commits than `routing.ci.maxAttempts` since it last passed: the session was told once to stop and escalate, and no further failure of the check is delivered until it passes (same fields as `ci.check_failed`; issue-462).
eventlog.event-type.ci.check_failed: A failing CI check was delivered to its session to heal, within its attempt budget (work_item, pull_request, check, attempt, max_attempts, head_sha; issue-462).
eventlog.event-type.cleanup.deferred: A work item closed but was NOT cleaned up, because the close event named no actor or an unauthorized one (work_item, reason: no-actor | unauthorized-actor, actor, closed_as, delivery_id). Fails closed on purpose: an authorized user's `the-loop cleanup` is the remedy (issue-186).
eventlog.event-type.config.reload-failed: A config edit could not be loaded and the previous configuration keeps running (path, error). Never stops an ingress on a bad edit (issue-496 R8.5).
eventlog.event-type.config.reloaded: A config edit was hot-reloaded into a running process (detail). The service emits it too when the edit changed WHICH ingresses it hosts (issue-395): detail names what was stopped and started.
eventlog.event-type.config.updated: The CLI config was changed through the control plane (path, keys). The **key paths** are recorded and the values are not: a value names people, hosts and binaries, and this trail is as readable as the event log is. issue-222.
eventlog.event-type.control.ambiguous: A comment opened lines with two or more different control keywords, so none was executed; the comment was routed as conversation (issue-498) (work_items, actor, commands).
eventlog.event-type.control.announce_fai: Mirroring a CLI control action to the work item failed (work_item, command, error) — best-effort; the command was still applied locally.
eventlog.event-type.control.announced: A CLI control action was mirrored to the work item as a comment carrying the same keyword (work_item, command).
eventlog.event-type.control.command: A control command was recognised and applied (work_item, command: start | stop | pause | resume | add-collaborator | remove-collaborator, source: comment | cli, actor, effect: spawned | resumed | paused | stopped | noop | granted | revoked | already-granted | not-a-collaborator) — the record of who asked for a run to start or stop, and (issue-307, with `collaborator`: the login) of who was invited onto a work item or removed from it. `loop` (issue-343) names the operator's own graph an arming command selected — a new command bound in `routing.control.commands` is logged as `start` with its `loop`.
eventlog.event-type.control.rejected: A control command was recognised but refused (work_items, command, source, actor, reason: spawn-policy | awaiting-start | nothing-to-resume | unauthorized-actor | missing-collaborator | input-refused: a lifecycle hook said no, issue-344) — e.g. a start for a work item that is not armed for autonomous execution (which is refused without being remembered), a command with no named authorized actor, or an `add-collaborator` naming no valid `@login`.
eventlog.event-type.diagnosis.deferred: Self-diagnosis hit the rolling daily cap (selfDiagnosis.maxIssuesPerDay) and left this candidate for a later scan (fingerprint, trigger). Deferred, not dropped.
eventlog.event-type.diagnosis.detected: Self-diagnosis (issue-242, opt-in) accepted a NEW failure fingerprint for diagnosis (fingerprint, trigger: the event type that raised it). Emitted once per fingerprint, on its first attempt.
eventlog.event-type.diagnosis.failed: A diagnosis attempt failed (fingerprint, trigger, stage: agent | post, attempt, error — scrubbed). Warning-level on purpose: diagnosis.* is excluded from candidacy, and the level makes that belt-and-braces. After selfDiagnosis.maxRetries failures the fingerprint is abandoned.
eventlog.event-type.diagnosis.posted: Self-diagnosis filed the issue (fingerprint, trigger, url) on the configured repository, labeled and self-authored — never armed.
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.abandoned: The dispatcher shut down with events still queued; they were never delivered and are left for the next start to retry (count, delivery_ids) — issue-159. On the poll path the attempts they spent are handed back (`poll.attempts_released`).
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.attachments: A forwarded GitHub event's body carried attachment URLs (issue-416): how many, and how many were fetched into the work item's attachment directory before the prompt was delivered (work_item, gh_event, count, fetched). A URL that was not fetched is named in the prompt with its reason; this line carries no URL and no path.
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.dropped: A routed event was discarded at dispatch (reason: duplicate-delivery | already-processed | spawn-policy | awaiting-start | session-paused | collaborator-no-spawn | session-vanished | no-adapter | session-occupied | work-item-not-found | no-work-item | ci-not-actionable | ci-autofix-exhausted | ci-review-loop | no-gate). `no-gate` (issue-488) is a quiz doorbell for a work item that is not waiting at a human gate — nothing to re-evaluate, and never a spawn. `ci-not-actionable` and `ci-autofix-exhausted` (issue-462) are the CI gate's (`routing.ci.autofix`): a CI event that needs no action (a running, passing, cancelled or aggregate one), or a failure of a check whose attempts are spent; both carry `check` and are settled, never retried. `ci-review-loop` (issue-524) is a CI event kept from a session walking the review loop, which changes no code: recorded per reviewer, carries `check`, and spends no attempt. `collaborator-no-spawn` (issue-307) means the event reached dispatch on a work-item collaborator grant, which admits input and never a new session. `work-item-not-found` (issue-269) means every work item the event named was a branch-invented ref the provider says does not exist, and `no-work-item` that it named none to begin with; in both cases the delivery id is deliberately NOT released, because that is a permanent condition and a redelivery could only reach the same answer. `session-occupied` (issue-146) means a dead tmux session held the work item's `loop-<slug>` name and could not be cleared, so nothing was spawned and the delivery id was deliberately NOT released — retrying could only hit the same collision. `awaiting-start` and `session-paused` are *suppressions*: the delivery id is kept AND recorded as settled (issue-270), so the poll path resolves the comment instead of counting a retry against it — nothing is replayed when the item is started or the session resumed, and the session reads the thread itself instead (`poll.comment_settled`).
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.error: A dispatch worker crashed on an event (work_item, error; will_retry).
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.failed: Delivering an event to its session failed (work_item, harness, error; will_retry: the delivery id was released so a redelivery / next poll cycle can retry).
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.queued: A routed event was enqueued on a session's FIFO queue (work_item, spawn: whether it will spawn a new session).
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.quiz_gate: A ticked quiz box re-evaluated the gate its work item waits at (issue-488): `outcome` is the gate's verdict. Delivery-only — no prompt is rendered or delivered, and nothing spawns.
eventlog.event-type.dispatch.succeeded: An event was delivered to its harness session (work_item, harness, via: resume | tmux; actor: the authorized user whose comment or review it was, absent for every other delivery — issue-551, where it starts a new nudge budget).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.bound: An instance published a binding — an object (a pull request, a Slack thread) belongs to a work item (instance, provider, key, ref, routed: how many held events it routed). Recorded so a binding that redirects a subject is never anonymous (issue-496, security review SEC-2).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.claimed: An instance published a claim on a subject (subject, instance, role, routed: how many held events the claim routed onto its queue).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.connected: The instance's gateway client reached the gateway (url, instance, peer), at start or after an outage.
eventlog.event-type.gateway.dropped: An ingress refused or discarded a delivery before storing it (provider, reason: bad-signature | replay-window | invalid-payload | unbound | undeclared-repository | duplicate, delivery_id). Nothing was stored.
eventlog.event-type.gateway.received: An ingress accepted a provider delivery (provider, source, kind, delivery_id, subject, event_id). Length-capped summary only; the payload is never logged.
eventlog.event-type.gateway.refused: The consumer API refused a request (instance, reason: duplicate-instance | duplicate-actor | duplicate-room | commit-undelivered | unknown-instance, holder, peer; channel for duplicate-room). On the client side the same event records the 409 it received, with `holder`.
eventlog.event-type.gateway.registered: An instance registered the actors it works for (instance, actors: counts per provider).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.released: An instance released its claim (subject, instance).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.reloaded: gateway-config.yaml was re-read and the enabled ingress set applied (detail).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.rooms: An instance published its rooms — the Slack collaboration channels its work items declared (instance, rooms: how many it now holds, routed: held events drained, refused: channels another live instance keeps) (issue-505).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.slack_call: The gateway made one Slack Web API call for an instance (instance, method, channel, status, ok) — issue-519. The pass-through: the call's text and the bot token never reach a line; a refused method or an unavailable posting is a gateway.refused instead.
eventlog.event-type.gateway.slack_downlo: The gateway fetched a message's file for an instance with its bot token (instance, host, status, size — or reason: off-host | over-cap | transfer-failed) — issue-519.
eventlog.event-type.gateway.started: The gateway process came up (listen, store, ingresses: the enabled set).
eventlog.event-type.gateway.unreachable: The instance's gateway client could not reach the gateway (url, error). Once per outage; the instance keeps running and never falls back to its own ingresses.
eventlog.event-type.graph.advanced: A work item's exit chain passed and the matching edge was taken (work_item, node, to, outcome).
eventlog.event-type.graph.assignment_del: The graph entered an agent node and pushed that node's assignment into the loop's bound session (work_item; endpoint: the PR's ref when an inner loop was assigned) — issue-172, the deliver-assignment entry hook. The graph assigns; the session works; the claim reports back.
eventlog.event-type.graph.assignment_fai: Pushing an entered node's assignment into its session failed (work_item, endpoint, error). Best-effort: the node is entered regardless, and the same state is re-rendered into every event prompt.
eventlog.event-type.graph.blocked: A node's exit chain was blocked by a hook; the node did not advance and the finding went back to the harness (work_item, node, hook).
eventlog.event-type.graph.cleaned: A work item entered the terminal `cleanup` node because the-loop was about to release its local resources (work_item, from: the node it stood on, reason) — issue-186. Not a force: no gate is bypassed and no verdict is claimed, so `check --recompute` still reports whatever never ran.
eventlog.event-type.graph.completed: A work item reached a terminal node (work_item, node).
eventlog.event-type.graph.escalated: A node exhausted its attempts, or repeated the same finding, and stopped advancing (work_item, node, attempts, repeated).
eventlog.event-type.graph.forced: An operator forced a transition regardless of gates — the escape hatch. The pointer moved; the bypassed gate keeps its real verdict, so `check --recompute` still reports it (work_item, from, to, actor, reason).
eventlog.event-type.graph.gate_session: A human gate was entered and its session resolved per `session: inherit` — inherited, or fresh-with-artifacts when the producing session is gone (work_item, node, resolution, session). issue-148.
eventlog.event-type.graph.hook_degraded: A best-effort hook passed the node while recording that its outbound call did not happen — a checklist not posted, a phase label not synced (work_item, node, hook, error). issue-194: the node's verdict and the edge taken are unaffected, which is the whole point of best-effort; what is NOT acceptable is a work item parked on a question the ticket never received. The CLI prints the same fact as a warning line; this is where the daemon's operator finds it.
eventlog.event-type.graph.link_failed: The ingress→graph coupling raised and was swallowed so the event was still delivered; the graph did not move (work_item, action, error). issue-113.
eventlog.event-type.graph.no_edge: No declared edge matched a node's outcome, so the work item was parked rather than guessed at (work_item, node, outcome).
eventlog.event-type.graph.node_skipped: The pointer routed around a declared-skipped node along its `on: skipped` edge — none of the node's hooks ran (work_item, node, plus the declaration's via/token/by/reason). issue-177. Distinct from graph.skipped, which is the ingress coupling declining to touch a graph at all.
eventlog.event-type.graph.opt_ins_select: A human selected one or more OPT-IN phases for a work item at the `phase-selection` gate (work_item, via: selection, nodes). The mirror of graph.skips_declared: those phases are off by default, so this is the record of somebody asking for them. issue-188.
eventlog.event-type.graph.outer_reevalua: The daemon re-ran the outer node's exit chain after an inner loop finished (work_item, node, status, outcome) — or declined to: outcome not-parked | no-inner-gate. A pass advances the work item exactly as a claim would (issue-538).
eventlog.event-type.graph.parked: A node is waiting on a human; its exit chain re-runs on the next inbound event (work_item, node).
eventlog.event-type.graph.pr_spec_record: `the-loop graph pr-spec` verified a pull request's PR spec and wrote its `pr-spec.json` record, or recorded that none is required (work_item, pull_request, findings, required). issue-543.
eventlog.event-type.graph.pr_spec_refuse: `the-loop graph pr-spec` found problems with a pull request's PR spec and wrote no record (work_item, pull_request, findings). issue-543.
eventlog.event-type.graph.pull_request_l: A pull request was recorded in the WORK ITEM's own checked-in state as delivering it (work_item, pull_request, via: session | event) — issue-368. The repository's half of the fact `session.pr_linked` records on this machine: a pull request is an object of the repository, so it travels on the work item's branch with its repository, number, URL, inner-loop directory and upstream state, instead of existing only in a session record that never leaves the machine that wrote it.
eventlog.event-type.graph.quiz_refused: A quiz box was ticked by someone who may not answer the gate, or by an editor GitHub could not name — the gate keeps waiting (work_item, node, editor, comment). issue-488 abuse case 1.
eventlog.event-type.graph.repos_declared: The agent declared which repositories this work item raises pull requests in (work_item, repos) — `the-loop graph repos`, called once design.md and tasks.md say what the change spans. `await-inner-loops` then holds `implementation` until each has an inner loop AND every started loop has finished. The flags are the full set, so this event is the whole declaration, not an addition to it. issue-365.
eventlog.event-type.graph.skipped: The ingress→graph coupling declined to touch a work item's graph, so a successful delivery moved nothing (work_item, action: start | advance, reason: no-spec-dir | spec-dir-outside-checkout, spec_dir: the directory `routing.graph.specDir` resolves to, default `docs/specs`). The answer to 'it is labelled, armed and spawned — why is its graph still at node one?'. issue-123, issue-352.
eventlog.event-type.graph.skips_declared: A human declared phases skipped for a work item — the `phase-selection` gate's authorized reply, or the `graph skip` verb (work_item, via: selection | cli, nodes; cli adds actor and reason). A declaration, never a verdict: `check` reports the nodes as skipped-by-declaration.
eventlog.event-type.graph.skips_rejected: A skip token was refused — unknown, outside the skip vocabulary, or (cli) naming a node the pointer already reached (work_item, token, via, why). The declaration never takes effect; the full process runs.
eventlog.event-type.graph.spec_tree_excl: A guest loop — a contribution or a review — started in a repository the-loop does not own, so its spec tree was written into the checkout's git exclude file — working state the contribution PR can never carry (work_item, path). issue-185, PR #187 review; keyed on the loop since issue-352.
eventlog.event-type.graph.started: A work item entered the graph's start node, running its entry chain (work_item, node). Emitted by the ingress coupling on spawn (issue-113) and by anything else calling `Runtime.start`.
eventlog.event-type.handoff.demoted: The import-handoff hook refused a carried artifact (missing, a sha256 mismatch, or a failed section check), so the runtime un-skipped the nodes from its producing node up to the record's enter node (work_item, nodes). The item starts earlier, never later; the refusal is in work-item-state.json's handoffDemoted.
eventlog.event-type.handoff.honoured: A GitHub issue not yet on the graph was armed with a handoff record (work_item, stage, enter, author, carried_by, branch, record): its checkout is made on the record's spec branch and Runtime.start freezes the record into work-item-state.json.
eventlog.event-type.handoff.ignored: One or more handoff records on a work item were not honoured (work_item, reasons: each record's URL and why — author not authorized, unknown version, malformed, item already on the graph). The item arms as one with no handoff.
eventlog.event-type.handoff.imported: `the-loop handoff import` materialized a handed-off item's carried files into its spec folder (work_item, written, refused: counts). Warning-level when any file was refused; the import-handoff hook then demotes the walk.
eventlog.event-type.handoff.unreadable: The comments of a work item being armed could not be listed, so no handoff record was read (work_item, error). Warning-level; the item arms as one with no handoff — fail closed, never a guessed stage.
eventlog.event-type.hooks.decided: A lifecycle hook changed a decision at a point (point, hook, changed: the decision fields whose value changed, work_item). Also emitted when a `required` hook's failure set proceed=false on its behalf.
eventlog.event-type.hooks.failed: A lifecycle hook raised, timed out, answered badly or could not be reached (point, hook, error, required, work_item). Warning-level: the chain continues with the context unchanged by that hook; a `required` hook at a point carrying `proceed` refuses the operation instead (see hooks.decided).
eventlog.event-type.hooks.load_failed: The `hooks` declaration could not be loaded and this process runs WITHOUT lifecycle hooks (error, strict=false). Warning-level: a one-shot command (`the-loop ask`, `the-loop graph complete`) proceeds hookless; a daemon started on the same config refuses to start instead.
eventlog.event-type.hooks.loaded: The top-level `hooks` declaration was loaded into this process (hooks: the names in order, count, config). Emitted only when at least one is declared.
eventlog.event-type.hooks.refused: A `proceed: false` decision was applied: a start was refused (work_item_start), a session launch was prevented (session_spawn), or a person's input was dropped (input_received: an answer, a comment, a control command) — point, reason, work_item, and the hook(s) that decided when known. The event is settled, the ticket gets one marked comment, nothing is retried.
eventlog.event-type.ingress.hosted: The control-plane service is hosting this ingress (poller | gh-webhook | slack-listener) as an in-process task (`service.hostIngresses`, issue-231). Its pidfile lock is held by the service's pid. `reason` is `startup`, or `config` when a config edit newly enabled it (issue-395).
eventlog.event-type.ingress.hosted_faile: An ENABLED ingress (poller | gh-webhook | slack-listener) did not start inside the control-plane service (ingress, reason). The service keeps serving, so the reason stays reachable over the API. Before issue-339 this was a logfile line and nothing else, so a poller that never came up was visible only as the absence of a `poller.started`.
eventlog.event-type.ingress.hosted_stopp: A hosted ingress was stopped by the service and its lock released (issue-231). `reason` is `shutdown`, or `config` when a config edit no longer enables it — a `read.mode: off` stops the listener without a restart (issue-395).
eventlog.event-type.instance.malformed: A member's answer was dropped (instance, operation, reason): oversized, not JSON, or not the shape the contract promises. The manager answers from the rest and never passes the body on.
eventlog.event-type.instance.mismatched: The host at a registered URL answers as a different instance (instance: the registered name, reported: the name it gave, role: the role it gave). Fail closed: nothing is served from it or sent to it until it answers to its name as a worker. At level error.
eventlog.event-type.instance.recovered: A registered instance answers to its name again (instance) after being unreachable or mismatched.
eventlog.event-type.instance.registered: An instance was added to this manager's registry (instance: its name) — through the API, the dashboard's Instances tab or `the-loop instances register`, all of which write `instance.manager.instances` through the same splice a hand edit would. The URL is not recorded: names only.
eventlog.event-type.instance.unreachable: A registered instance stopped answering (instance, reason) — a transport failure or a timeout on its probe. Once per transition, at level error; its rows are left out of every list read until `instance.recovered`.
eventlog.event-type.instance.unregistere: An instance was removed from this manager's registry (instance).
eventlog.event-type.mcp.call: An MCP tool call was served over the control-plane's HTTP endpoint (tool, ok). Same authorization and audit trail as the REST surface.
eventlog.event-type.poll.attempts_releas: A shutdown returned the retry budget of dispatches that were still queued and never delivered (released) — issue-159, so restarting the poller does not accumulate toward `polling.maxRetries`.
eventlog.event-type.poll.closure_detecte: A poll cycle found that a tracked work item — one with a session record of any status, or a portable record that is armed, frozen or has a roster — or a ledger-only record absent from the listing for a window (issue-332) had ended upstream and closed it (work_item, state: closed | merged, kind); only ever after a successful listing, never on an unanswerable state, and never twice for a stamped record (issue-94, issue-329).
eventlog.event-type.poll.comment_failed: The poller gave up forwarding a comment after exhausting the retry budget (polling.maxRetries); later polls ignore it (work_item, comment_id, actor, attempts, will_retry=False).
eventlog.event-type.poll.comment_forward: A new authorized comment was forwarded to the item's session (work_item, comment_id, actor, attempt: which retry this was).
eventlog.event-type.poll.comment_settled: A forwarded comment was resolved because the dispatcher is FINISHED with its delivery, not because it was delivered (work_item, comment_id, actor, outcome: awaiting-start | session-paused | collaborator-no-spawn | control-executed | control-rejected | parked-at-human-start-gate | mirror-refused | addressed-elsewhere | unaddressed | instance-locked | ambiguous-address | ci-not-actionable | ci-autofix-exhausted | ci-review-loop, will_retry=False) — issue-270. (The three `ci-*` outcomes are the CI gate's, issue-462 and issue-524: settled CI events. The poller lists no CI, so they complete the dispatcher's vocabulary rather than occur here today.) Either the event was suppressed on purpose (the work item is not started, or its session is paused), or it WAS a control command, executed here and never forwarded, or its start was accepted and parked at a human gate (issue-449), or (issue-322) it was outside THIS instance's scope — another instance may own the work item, so the refusal is final and leaves no mark. The comment is baselined rather than retried or abandoned: it is not written to `gaveUp`, so no later version re-arms it, and nothing is replayed when the item is started or resumed — a spawned session reads the thread itself, which the spawn prompt tells it to do.
eventlog.event-type.poll.cycle: One poll cycle finished (items_seen, spawns, comments_forwarded, closures, errors; scopes_polled and scopes_degraded — the repositories that answered, and the ones that failed or were skipped, issue-315; ledger_checks — how many ledger-only records were asked whether they ended, issue-332; ci_forwarded — how many new CI results from `polling.ci` were handed to the dispatcher's CI gate, issue-462).
eventlog.event-type.poll.giveup_report_f: The give-up notice could not be posted — no `gh` on PATH, a non-GitHub work item, or an API error (work_item, comment_id, error). Best-effort: the give-up itself is recorded regardless.
eventlog.event-type.poll.giveup_reported: A give-up (`poll.comment_failed`) was reported on the work item, so the human who wrote the comment learns it never reached the session (work_item, comment_id, attempts) — issue-240.
eventlog.event-type.poll.item_error: Processing one polled work item failed; retried next cycle (work_item, error, will_retry).
eventlog.event-type.poll.item_filtered: A listed item lacked required arming labels (item_number, required_labels, missing_labels, reason). Every configured label is required.
eventlog.event-type.poll.provider_error: Asking a provider for its work items failed; retried next cycle (provider, error, will_retry).
eventlog.event-type.poll.rearmed: Comments abandoned by a spent retry budget under a DIFFERENT the-loop version were un-resolved for one more full budget (work_item, comments, version) — issue-146, so a work item stranded by a bug an upgrade fixed is picked up instead of staying stuck. Never emitted for a give-up the running version recorded.
eventlog.event-type.poll.scope_degraded: A scope's listing failed with a condition no retry changes — for GitHub, a repository whose Issues are disabled. Surfaced ONCE, at warning level: the poller stops asking it for issues (its pull requests are still polled), re-probes it every retry_after_cycles cycles, on a config reload and on restart, and `the-loop status` shows it as degraded meanwhile (provider, scope, error, retry_after_cycles) — issue-315.
eventlog.event-type.poll.scope_error: One scope of a source — a repository, for GitHub — could not be listed; the source's other scopes were still polled, and nothing in this one is reconciled as closed (provider, scope, error, will_retry=True) — issue-315. Before it, one repository's failure was the whole provider's, and every repository stopped being polled.
eventlog.event-type.poll.scope_recovered: A degraded scope answered again on a re-probe and is polled normally (provider, scope) — issue-315.
eventlog.event-type.poll.spawn_failed: The poller gave up spawning a session for an item after exhausting the retry budget (polling.maxRetries); later polls ignore it until new activity re-arms it (work_item, attempts, will_retry=False).
eventlog.event-type.poll.unauthorized: A polled item was not started by the poller itself: its author is not an authorized user and nobody has armed it. Its comments are still acted on, judged by their own authors (work_item, actor).
eventlog.event-type.poller.blocked: A poller refused to start because another one already holds the single-instance lock on the state root (pidfile, holder) — issue-159. Two pollers on one ledger interleave read-modify-write and re-forward each other's comments, so the second one does not run.
eventlog.event-type.reaction.added: A dispatch-lifecycle emoji reaction was added to the triggering comment/issue/PR (work_item, state: started | completed | error, content, target) — issue-84, routing.reactions.
eventlog.event-type.reaction.failed: Adding a dispatch-lifecycle reaction failed; the dispatch itself is unaffected (work_item, state, content, error).
eventlog.event-type.restart.completed: A `the-loop restart` finished (ok, withUpgrade): every running service stopped, the optional CLI upgrade ran, every enabled service started. Per-service outcomes are in the command's output/logfile. issue-228.
eventlog.event-type.restart.scheduled: A whole-system restart was scheduled (issue-228): a detached `the-loop restart` was spawned (pid, logfile, withUpgrade). Emitted by POST /api/v1/restart — the service cannot stop itself synchronously and still answer, so the API's contract is scheduling.
eventlog.event-type.routing.collaborator: A verified event was routed on a WORK-ITEM COLLABORATOR grant rather than `routing.authorizedUsers` (gh_event, actor, work_items) — issue-307. An authorized user granted this login the right to be *input* on these work items: the comment reaches the session, and the control and spawn seams still refuse it everything else.
eventlog.event-type.routing.dropped: A verified event was not routed (reason: disabled-event | duplicate-delivery | undeclared-repository | no-work-item | unauthorized-actor; actor). `undeclared-repository` (issue-348) is the repository bound: the delivery — or a work item it named — is outside the top-level `repositories`, the one list every ingress reads. It carries `repository` for a delivery judged on its own repository and `work_items` for refs filtered out of one, and is checked ABOVE the actor guard, so an undeclared repository's payload reaches nothing else.
eventlog.event-type.routing.linkage_drop: A work-item ref an event named ONLY through the issue-<n> branch convention does not exist, so it was removed from that event's work items before anything acted on it (work_item, source: branch, reason: not-found, gh_event, delivery_id) — issue-269. The branch convention is the one linkage source that supplies a repository the event never stated; every other source is routed unchecked.
eventlog.event-type.routing.routed: A verified event mapped to work item(s) and passed all guards (gh_event, work_items, labeled).
eventlog.event-type.server.started: The webhook receiver started (host, port, path, routing).
eventlog.event-type.service.started: The control-plane API service came up (host, port).
eventlog.event-type.service.stopped: The control-plane API service shut down.
eventlog.event-type.session.announce_fai: Posting the tmux-session announcement comment failed (work_item, tmux_target, error) — best-effort, the dispatch is unaffected.
eventlog.event-type.session.announced: A comment announcing a newly spawned tmux session (and how to attach to it) was posted on the work item (work_item, tmux_target); a respawn reuses the name and posts nothing further.
eventlog.event-type.session.ask_answered: An authorized person's comment was delivered to a session that had an open ask, which closes the ask and cancels its default (work_item, ask_id, actor) — issue-551. Written by the dispatcher on delivery only: a comment it refuses writes nothing, so an unauthorized reply never stops a default.
eventlog.event-type.session.ask_default_: An ask's default was taken because nobody answered by its deadline (work_item, ask_id, default) — issue-551. The session was told to proceed with its own default, and the work item's thread says so. Written once per ask; no gate reads it, so a default never counts as a person's answer.
eventlog.event-type.session.ask_reminded: An ask with no default went unanswered for `routing.asks.reminderSeconds`, and one reminder was posted on its thread (work_item, ask_id) — issue-551. Once per ask.
eventlog.event-type.session.autoclosed: A session was auto-closed because its work item ended (work_item, reason: issue-closed | pr-merged | pr-closed; merged: the closure is a merge, or a pull request recorded on the work item merged — issue-405; waited_seconds, finished: only when the closure was first held for the session's endgame, whether the completion claim ended the hold).
eventlog.event-type.session.awaiting_inp: A session asked a human a question through `the-loop ask` and is now waiting for the answer (work_item, question, actor, comment_url, comment_posted: whether the question reached the ticket, channels_posted: how many channels took it — 0 means nobody was paged and the outbox holds it, issue-409; ask_id: this ask's own id, default: the default answer when one was given, default_at: when it is taken when a wait was given — issue-551) — issue-208. The verb stamps the loop-prevention marker centrally, so the wait is recorded even when the agent forgot nothing. Closed by the next session.reply_sent, session.ask_answered (an authorized answer given on the ticket) or session.ask_default_taken.
eventlog.event-type.session.choice_chang: A session was re-launched (resuming its conversation) because the model or effort its work item resolves to no longer matches what the session was launched with (issue-358, R4.3) — a choice changed after the gate, a declaration withdrawn, or a verdict that turned `refused` (work_item, harness, previous_model, previous_effort).
eventlog.event-type.session.choice_refus: A model or effort level a work item had frozen was withheld because this machine's harness refuses it (issue-358, R7.4). The session is launched on the harness's own arguments instead, and the choice is not retried until its verdict changes (work_item, harness, kind, name).
eventlog.event-type.session.cleaned: A work item's LOCAL resources were released — `the-loop cleanup`, the same verb from the CLI/API, or a closure by an authorized user (work_item, actor, source: comment | cli | close-event, removed: which of tmux|workspace|session went, endpoints: the conversations ended, found: false when there was nothing here, error). The PORTABLE record — control, poll, graph — is deliberately untouched, and nothing remote is changed (issue-186).
eventlog.event-type.session.closed: A session was closed in the registry (work_item).
eventlog.event-type.session.closing: A work item ended while its session stands on the graph's terminal node — the endgame, where the completion summary is posted and `graph complete` claimed — so the closure is HELD rather than run (work_item, reason, node, grace_seconds, delivery_id; issue-405 P2). The session's claim ends the hold; routing.tmux.finishGraceSeconds ends it regardless; `session.autoclosed` then records how it ended.
eventlog.event-type.session.closing_canc: A held closure was dropped because the work item was reopened during the hold (work_item, source); the session stays live (issue-405 P2).
eventlog.event-type.session.credentials_: A spawned or respawned session was handed opted-in credentials from `env.sessionCredentials` (work_item, tmux_target, names) — issue-533. Warning level on purpose: an unattended agent now holds a token. Names only, never a value.
eventlog.event-type.session.default_harn: The declared default cannot host a session; the routing fallback was used (declared_harness, harness, reason).
eventlog.event-type.session.harness_term: The harness process inside a retained tmux session was ended when the work item closed, so the pane stays readable but can no longer be typed into (work_item, harness, tmux_target, ok, error) — routing.tmux.killHarnessOnClose: false skips it.
eventlog.event-type.session.identity_bou: The launch identity was resolved to the harness's native conversation id (work_item, harness, harness_session_id).
eventlog.event-type.session.kept_open: A close event matched a session only through linkage — one of the work item's PRs closed, the work item itself did not — so the session was left active (work_item, reason, closed_ref, delivery_id); a work item may be delivered by several PRs (issue-101).
eventlog.event-type.session.link_failed: Recording a pull request against its work item failed (work_item, linked_ref, error). Best-effort: the event was still dispatched, and routing falls back to deriving the linkage as it did before issue-172.
eventlog.event-type.session.nudged: The watcher told an idle session to continue (work_item, stall_id, node, nudge: its number within this visit to the node) — issue-551. The text is a fixed prompt naming the node and its command, nothing else. At most `routing.watchdog.maxNudges` per node visit.
eventlog.event-type.session.paused: A session was paused, so events for its work item are held rather than delivered (work_item, harness, harness_session_id) — issue-106, the pause command.
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_closed: A pull request's endpoint was closed while its work item's session kept running (work_item, pull_request) — a work item may be delivered by several PRs, so one merging ends only that conversation (issue-101, issue-172).
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_linked: A pull request was durably recorded as delivering a work item (work_item, pull_request) — issue-172. Written when the routing decision is made, so which session owns the PR's events stops being recomputed from `gh` — and, since issue-274, by the session that OPENED the pull request (`sessions link-pr`), which is the only writer a the-loop-authored PR has: it carries no closing reference, no `issue-<n>` branch and no closing keyword to infer from. Emitted only when the PR is newly listed.
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_notice_de: The work item's own session was told that one of its pull requests' sessions changed state (work_item, pull_request, transition, via: paste | with-event) — spawned, declined, spawn-failed, respawned, respawn-failed, completed, merged, closed or escalated (issue-538).
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_notice_fa: Pasting a pull-request session notice into the work item's session failed (work_item, pull_request, transition, error). Not retried; the path it rode on carried on (issue-538).
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_notice_sk: A pull-request session notice was not delivered because the work item has no session to tell (work_item, pull_request, transition, reason: paused | no-live-session). The inner state files still hold the fact (issue-538).
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_session_d: A pull request was NOT given a session of its own, and its event went into the work item's session instead (work_item, pull_request, reason: no-separate-checkout | workspace-failed | shared-worktree) — issue-253. An endpoint gets a conversation only when it has a working tree of its own; without `routing.workspace.root` there is none to give, and two harness sessions never share a tree. Under `sessionPerPr: always` a same-repository endpoint is also declined (reason workspace-failed) when its checkout cannot hold the pull request's head branch — which is every time the work item's own session already holds it under `workspace.strategy: worktree`.
eventlog.event-type.session.pr_spawned: A recorded pull request got its own tmux session and harness conversation (work_item, pull_request, harness, harness_session_id, tmux_target; harness_args, the argv it launched with, since issue-377) — `routing.tmux.sessionPerPr`. The work item's own session is untouched; this is an additional endpoint. Which pull requests reach this is the operator's choice (issue-258): under the default `cross-repository` only one in ANOTHER repository does, because the work item's own repository is its own session's; `always` adds same-repository pull requests that can be given a checkout of their own; `never` reaches this for none of them.
eventlog.event-type.session.registered: A work item ↔ harness session link was recorded in the registry (work_item, harness, harness_session_id, cwd).
eventlog.event-type.session.reply_sent: An operator's answer was delivered straight into the waiting session's tmux pane via POST /api/v1/sessions/reply (work_item, actor) — issue-208. Closes the work item's session.awaiting_input on the attention surface and the dashboard alike.
eventlog.event-type.session.reset: A work item's state on this machine was reset — `the-loop sessions reset` (work_item, actor, removed: which of workspace|session|control|poll went, found: false when there was nothing here, was_live, error). Appended like every other event: a reset can never erase its own trail.
eventlog.event-type.session.respawn_aver: A delivery reported its tmux session missing, but the session turned out to be alive when the respawn re-checked — so the pending event was delivered into the existing session and nothing was respawned (work_item, harness, tmux_target, gh_event, delivery_id). issue-146: the-loop never spawns over a live `loop-<slug>`; it routes into it.
eventlog.event-type.session.respawned: A tmux-mode session found dead on delivery was respawned on a fresh tmux session, and the pending event delivered as its boot prompt (work_item, harness, harness_session_id, runner, tmux_target, resumed: whether the previous conversation was resumed or a fresh one started, gh_event, delivery_id; harness_args, model, effort as on session.spawned).
eventlog.event-type.session.restart_fail: A relaunch did not produce a running harness (work_item, harness, tmux_target, error): tmux refused the respawn, or the resumed harness exited inside the probe window. The session is left as it was found.
eventlog.event-type.session.restarted: A running session was relaunched in place onto the environment `env.file` declares now (work_item, harness, tmux_target, outcome, stale) — issue-410's recovery from a credential rotation. `outcome` is restarted / stale / unverified, and `stale` names the variables that STILL differ afterwards, never their values.
eventlog.event-type.session.resume_faile: A respawn could not resume the dead session's conversation and fell back to a fresh one (work_item, harness, harness_session_id, error) — e.g. an unresumable id or a harness without interactive resume. Not emitted when resuming is simply off (routing.tmux.resumeOnRespawn).
eventlog.event-type.session.resumed: A paused session returned to active and delivery resumed (work_item, harness, harness_session_id); events suppressed while paused are not replayed.
eventlog.event-type.session.retained: A closed work item's tmux session was left running so its transcript stays readable (work_item, tmux_target); routing.tmux.keepSessionOnClose: false kills it instead.
eventlog.event-type.session.spawn_deferr: No session was spawned, on purpose: the work item is parked on its graph's first node and that node is a HUMAN gate the daemon services itself (issue-358, R8) — `phase-selection`, a contribution's `goal-definition`. A session starts once an authorized reply unparks the pointer, and it then carries the model that gate froze (work_item, harness, gh_event, delivery_id, reason).
eventlog.event-type.session.spawn_failed: Spawning a session failed (work_item, harness, error; will_retry).
eventlog.event-type.session.spawned: A new harness session was spawned for a work item — this is the 'what triggered this session' record (work_item, harness, harness_session_id, runner, gh_event, delivery_id; and, since issue-377, the argv it was launched with: harness_args, model, effort, each omitted when empty — so 'was it launched with the flag?' is answerable from the log alone).
eventlog.event-type.session.stall_ended: A stalled session took a turn again (work_item, stall_id, idle_seconds) — issue-551. Only a turn's start ends a stall; the stall notice is edited to say so.
eventlog.event-type.session.stalled: A session stayed idle with work owed after its nudges were spent, and a person is told once (work_item, stall_id: the work item and the time the idle period began, node, idle_since) — issue-551.
eventlog.event-type.session.turn_ended: A session's turn ended and the Stop gate allowed it (work_item, node, node_status, reason: human-gate | complete | exit-met | graph-wait | open-ask | declared-wait | background-work | inconclusive | gate-gave-up) — issue-551. The reason decides whether the session now waits or is idle.
eventlog.event-type.session.turn_started: A session's harness started a turn (work_item, node) — issue-551. Written by the turn-start hook; while it is a session's last turn record the session is working and the watcher leaves it alone.
eventlog.event-type.session.wait_declare: A session declared with `the-loop wait` what it waits for and until when (work_item, condition, until) — issue-551. Covers the one stop that ends the turn it was made in, and is refused over `routing.watchdog.maxWaitSeconds` and on a human-owned node.
eventlog.event-type.session.work_item_mi: The session announcement came back 404: the work item the-loop just spawned a session for does not exist (work_item, tmux_target, error) — issue-269. Recorded, not acted on: a repository the credential cannot see answers 404 for items that do exist, so killing a live session on this evidence would destroy work. The ref is remembered as missing, so the next event naming it through a branch convention is dropped.
eventlog.event-type.standing.announce_fa: A standing session's Slack announcement did not land (standing, error). Best-effort by contract: the session is up regardless, it simply has no Slack thread.
eventlog.event-type.standing.announced: A standing session was announced in Slack and the resulting thread bound to it (standing, channel, thread), which is what makes replies in that thread reach its terminal.
eventlog.event-type.standing.create_fail: A create wrote its record but the session would not start (standing, error); the record was removed again, so the name is free for a retry.
eventlog.event-type.standing.created: A standing session was brought into existence through the API rather than declared in the config (standing, harness, cwd, auto_start) — issue-277 R6. The definition now lives in its registry record.
eventlog.event-type.standing.deleted: A created standing session was stopped and its record removed (standing). Unlike standing.stopped, nothing comes back: the conversation id is gone with the record.
eventlog.event-type.standing.resume_fail: A standing session's resume did not survive its liveness probe (standing, harness_session_id, error); a fresh conversation is started instead, so a standing.started follows.
eventlog.event-type.standing.resumed: A standing session was spawned continuing its RECORDED conversation rather than a fresh one (same payload as standing.started), which is what makes `the-loop restart` not amnesia for a supervisor session.
eventlog.event-type.standing.said: A message was pasted into a running standing session and submitted (standing, tmux_target, actor). Nothing is posted to any ticket — there is none — so this event is the delivery's only record.
eventlog.event-type.standing.spawn_faile: A standing session could not be started (standing, harness, tmux_target, error): a missing harness binary, a cwd that is not there, an unreadable promptFile, or a live tmux session the-loop has no record of and will not spawn over.
eventlog.event-type.standing.started: A standing session — one that belongs to no work item — was spawned on a fresh conversation (standing, harness, harness_session_id, tmux_target, cwd). issue-277.
eventlog.event-type.standing.stop_failed: A standing session's tmux session could not be killed (standing, tmux_target, error); the record is marked stopped regardless.
eventlog.event-type.standing.stopped: A standing session's harness was terminated and its tmux session killed (standing, tmux_target). The record is KEPT, so the next start resumes the same conversation.
eventlog.event-type.stream.desync: A subscriber was told to refetch everything rather than served a partial history (reason: truncated | rotated | replay-window | queue-overflow). Not an error — the self-healing path — but the signal that the log was rotated under the service, or that a client is reading slower than the workstation emits.
eventlog.event-type.stream.disconnected: A subscriber's connection ended (frames: how many were delivered, reason: client | shutdown). The slot is released, and the tailer stops when the last subscriber leaves.
eventlog.event-type.stream.refused: A stream connection was refused and never accepted (reason: disabled | at-capacity | bad-cursor | bad-filter, subscribers). `at-capacity` means `service.stream.maxSubscribers` is reached — the bound that keeps an open dashboard from starving the REST surface; the others are caller errors, refused rather than widened to an unfiltered stream.
eventlog.event-type.stream.subscribed: A client opened GET /api/v1/stream (subscribers: how many are now open, work_items / transcripts: the filters it asked for, cursor: where it resumed from, or absent for a fresh connection). The answer to 'who is watching this workstation?'.
eventlog.event-type.subject.appended: An event was stored on a subject (event_id, subject, provider, kind, delivery_id). Written BEFORE the provider is acknowledged.
eventlog.event-type.subject.committed: An instance committed a delivery (instance, seq, event_id, outcome).

eventlog.event-type.subject.expired: Retention dropped an uncommitted delivery or a held event (subject, event_id, instance, age_s).
eventlog.event-type.subject.redelivered: A fetch returned a delivery again (instance, seq, event_id, attempt): the previous attempt was never committed.
eventlog.event-type.subject.routed: The stored event's consumers were resolved (event_id, subject, to: the instance list, or `unassigned` when none; by: claim | actor | hold | binding | room | late, when a binding or room published between the resolve and the append routed it).
eventlog.event-type.webhook.received: An inbound webhook POST was accepted for routing (gh_event, delivery_id, verified: HMAC signature checked).
eventlog.event-type.webhook.rejected: An inbound webhook POST was refused before routing (reason: invalid-signature | invalid-payload).
eventlog.event-type.work_item.commented: The agent's comment was posted on a work item through `the-loop comment` (work_item, comment_url, comment_posted, channels_posted) — marked and enveloped by the ledger, so no ingress re-publishes it. `warning` when the post failed.
eventlog.event-type.work_item.ended: A work item ended upstream and its portable record was stamped `ended` (work_item, state: closed | merged, kind: issue | pull-request, reason: issue-closed | pr-merged | pr-closed, outcome: completed | cancelled | closed-externally | unknown — issue-452, source: webhook | poll, actor: who closed it or none, delivery_id). Written with or without a session on this machine; the attention surfaces read it to demote the item (issue-329), and `the-loop check <ref>` answers from its terminal record once the checkout is gone.
eventlog.event-type.work_item.merge_refu: `the-loop pr merge` refused to merge (pull_request, reason): the executing process's `routing.mergeOnApproval` is false — a person merges this repository's pull requests — or the pull request is not recorded against a work item registered on this instance.
eventlog.event-type.work_item.pr_labelle: Every `routing.autoExecuteLabels` label was put on a pull request the-loop had just linked to a work item (pull_request, labels) — `pr create`, `sessions link-pr` and its `--discover` (issue-466), so the poller, which lists only a PR carrying all of them, sees it. `warning` with `error` when GitHub refused or the host is untrusted; the link stands either way.
eventlog.event-type.work_item.pr_merged: `the-loop pr merge` merged a pull request (pull_request, method).
eventlog.event-type.work_item.pr_opened: `the-loop pr create` opened a pull request for a work item (work_item, pull_request, url); the link that follows is its own `session.pr_linked`.
eventlog.event-type.work_item.pr_ready: `the-loop pr ready` took a registered work item's draft pull request out of draft, ready for review (pull_request; issue-465).
eventlog.event-type.work_item.pull_reque: A pull request delivering a tracked work item merged or closed (work_item: the owner, pull_request, state: merged | closed) — issue-368. The pull request's upstream state is recorded in the work item's own state file and its poll ledger is dropped from the owner's portable record. No `ended` stamp and no record of its own: a pull request that delivers a work item is not a work item.
eventlog.event-type.work_item.reopened: A work item's `ended` stamp was cleared because the item is open again (work_item, source: webhook — a `reopened` event — or poll — the item was listed) (issue-329).
eventlog.event-type.work_item.thread_res: `the-loop pr resolve-thread` resolved one review thread of a pull request recorded against a registered work item (pull_request, thread).
eventlog.event-type.work_item.ticket_clo: `the-loop ticket close` closed a registered work item's ticket (work_item, reason: completed | not_planned).
eventlog.event-type.workspace.cleaned: A work item's checkout was removed — when its session closed, or when its local resources were released by `the-loop cleanup` (work_item, strategy). Uncommitted work in that checkout went with it.
eventlog.event-type.workspace.prepared: A per-work-item checkout was made ready for a spawned session (work_item, strategy: worktree | clone, checkout, branch).
eventlog.event-type.workspace.trust_fail: Pre-seeding the harness's config failed (work_item, harness, cwd, error); the spawn still proceeds, but the session may stop on an interactive dialog or run without the-loop's plugin.
eventlog.event-type.workspace.trusted: A spawned session's environment was pre-seeded in the harness's own config so it starts unattended and with the loop loaded — workspace trust, the bypass-permissions disclaimer when that mode is configured, and the-loop's own plugin (work_item, harness, cwd, applied) — issue-90 / routing.harnessTrust, issue-143 / routing.harnessPlugins.
